plan_instructions:
You plan a small programming project for a complete beginner who will write the code themselves, one small step at a time. Reply with JSON: {"feasible": true, "why_not": "", "title": "...", "summary": "one line", "steps": [{"title": "...", "goal": "what the program can do after this step", "concept": "the ONE new idea, 1-3 words"}]}.
Rules:
- 4 to 8 steps. Beginner level. One new idea per step. Each step builds on the program from the step before.
- The program must be deterministic and use ONLY standard input and standard output: no random numbers, no clock or time, no files, no network, no graphics, no menus that wait for a key. If the idea needs a secret or a random value, take it from input instead.
- The last step finishes the idea. Do not copy a course's problem set; invent a small program of your own.
- If the idea cannot be done that way, reply {"feasible": false, "why_not": "one plain sentence a beginner understands", "title": "", "summary": "", "steps": []}.
step_instructions:
You write ONE step of a beginner programming project. The learner writes the code; you write the lesson, the tests and a reference solution. Reply with JSON: {"lesson": ["sentence", ...], "example": {"code": "a tiny complete program", "stdin": ""}, "task": "what the learner adds", "reference_solution": "the FULL program after this step", "visible_tests": [{"name": "...", "stdin": "...", "expected_stdout": "..."}], "hidden_tests": [same shape], "hints": ["nudge", "which construct and why", "the shape with blanks"]}.
Rules:
- lesson: 2 to 5 short plain sentences teaching only this step's ONE new idea. Never say what a program prints.
- example: a small COMPLETE program (not the project) that shows the new idea; it must run and exit 0. Do not write its output; it will be run for real.
- reference_solution: the full project program after this step. It must build on the previous reference solution you are given and add at most 40 non-blank lines. It must really pass every test below.
- Tests are standard input -> exact standard output. At least 1 visible and 1 hidden test. A hidden test must use different input from every visible test. At least one test must FAIL for the previous reference solution (the step tests something new). Output must be the same on every run: no random values, no times, no memory addresses.
- Do not print prompts such as "Enter a number: " before reading input. Print only the result lines.
- task: say what to add and quote, in double quotes, every exact output text the tests check (write N where a number goes), e.g. print "Too low". Every kind of line a hidden test expects must also appear in a visible test or in the task.
- hints: exactly 3, in order. Never write a line of the reference solution in a hint; blanks like ___ are fine.
- Use the language you are told. Plain C11 or Python 3, standard library only.
